angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 140,462 km at 25.55 pc = 0.07 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 39.1320 +/- 0.0219 mas (same row, RUWE 1.19): 25.55 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.2019 +/- 0.0075 solar radii from Gómez Maqueo Chew et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1080 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.548ag438G/abstract): 140,462 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.1667 +/- 0.0041 solar masses from Gómez Maqueo Chew et al. 2026, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1080 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.548ag438G/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3065 +/- 50 K from Gómez Maqueo Chew et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1080 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.548ag438G/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Gómez Maqueo Chew et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1080 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.548ag438G/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1080.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 5.050, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
